On overlaps these vector measures represent the same intrinsic indicator derivative. Local Radon uniqueness identifies them. Partitioning unit normal values into finitely many small spherical caps proves total variation equals the scalar graph measure, so its compatibility is proved rather than presumed from a smooth area theorem.

Finite graph charts with bounded Jacobian give area at most Cr² in every small ball. Compact subchart margins and vertical gap at most (1+L)δ give tube volume O(δ). Matching traces cancel the first-order interface distributions, so no artificial delta derivative remains. Bounded Lipschitz cutoff multiplication is justified by the near/far Slobodeckij split, and chart transitions use intrinsic surface measure with bounded graph densities and bi-Lipschitz distances. Local lifts carry χ_jg and an ambient cutoff equal to one on that support, so their traces sum to g rather than to a sum of squared cutoffs. Ordinary extension is supplied independently, avoiding a circular trace-to-extension argument. Compact localization plus the L6 homogeneous bound gives the dot-H1 trace.

The transmission pair gives U in global L6 and piecewise H1 boundary collars. First-order Green produces distributional grad U equal to piecewise grad plus φ n δΓ, and stationarity yields −ΔU acting as integral φ∂nη. The source-normal derivative of the Newton fundamental solution has the same action; no derivative of the a.e. normal is taken. |∂nG|≤C|x−y|^(−2) is locally volume integrable, giving P in L1loc and its ball integral at most CR||φ||1. Off the compact boundary the integral is absolutely convergent and smooth. The difference U−P is distributionally entire harmonic; mollification and the ball mean-value formula give its value at most C(R^(−1/2)||U||6+R^(−2)||φ||1), tending to zero. Thus U=P without an unstated Weyl or exterior decay theorem. No planar-face assertion enters this chain.
